newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Fresh gains for Wall Street stocks and a firmer bond market gave Dutch shares a late push into record territory on Monday.
The AEX index of 25 blue chips closed 4.39 points or 0.74 percent higher at 597.10, beating the previous record close of 594.33 set on October 18.
Dealers said the Dutch market shrugged off a slightly weaker dollar, normally a bearish factor for Amsterdam, to outperform Frankfurt and London.
"The lower dollar didn't seem to hurt us at all and that indicates that there just aren't any sellers," said one dealer.
Index heavyweights ABN AMRO, ING and Royal Dutch -- each with a maximum weighting of around 10 percent in the AEX -- provided the main thrust of Monday's gains.
Financial issues ABN AMRO and ING were buoyed by firmer bonds. ABN AMRO was 1.50 guilders firmer at 101.00 -- its first ever close above 100.00. ING was up one guilder at 57.20.
Royal Dutch Petroleum gained 4.50 guilders at 277.80 on continuing oil price firmness.
Some dealers believe the AEX is now poised to break through the 600 level in the coming days.
"I think we should see a close above 600 on Tuesday unless something goes badly wrong on Wall Street or with the dollar," said one trader.
Chartists taking part in a weekly Reuter poll have moved to a mainly bullish stance from a neutral stance a week ago.
